## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Asitābhūjātaka* (Ja 234) is a canonical Jātaka narrative included in the *Khuddakanikāya* of the Pali Tipiṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The narrative opens in the present with the Buddha residing at the Jetavana monastery near Sāvatthī, where he delivers the discourse in connection with a young woman (*aññataram kumārikam ārabbha*) [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1879]. The verse text begins with the line *Tvam eva dānim akarā ti* [Fausböll 1879]. In the story of the past, the narrative concerns the royal daughter Asitābhū (*Asitābhu rājadhītā*) and a prince; in the resolution (*samodhāna*), the Buddha identifies the ascetic of the past as himself, while the prince and princess are identified as the figures of the present narrative [Fausböll 1879].
In the second volume of V. Fausböll's critical edition of the *Jātaka Together with Its Commentary*, the text is edited as the fourth tale in its section, placed between the *Vikaṇṇakajātaka* (Ja 233) and the *Vacchanakhajātaka* (Ja 235) [Fausböll 1879]. SuttaCentral does not list any cross-language parallels in Chinese, Tibetan, or Sanskrit collections [SuttaCentral]. In DharmaNexus's text-reuse analysis, no cross-language alignments meet the reporting threshold, while Pali-internal reuse is detected exclusively with the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (7 matching passages, up to 470 characters in common; longest match §0.4–1.4 aligned with §1467_12–1470) [DharmaNexus].
